overview: Black mirrors White's fianchetto with 1...b6, so both sides plan Bb2/Bb7 and slowly build a centre. White usually plays 2.Bb2 Bb7 3.e3 Nf6 and then Nf3, d4 or c4 depending on Black's set-up. The game is a quiet manoeuvring battle where small differences in centre control decide.

white_ideas.idea: Bb2, e3, Nf3 and a choice of d4 or c4 to build a centre.
Use the long diagonal and trade the opposing bishop to gain space.

black_ideas.idea: Mirror the set-up with ...Bb7, ...e6 and ...Nf6, contesting the centre by ...c5 or ...d5.
Challenge the b2 bishop with ...Bxg2 trades or pawn breaks.

typical_structures.structure: Mirror-image fianchetto structures with a flexible centre and bishops facing each other.

structure.notes: Flank opening with an undecided centre.

approach.notes: Played by strong players now and then; standard, though more of a set-up than a theory line.

level.notes: Fianchetto plans are easy to follow; little theory.

character.reason: Symmetrical, quiet, neither forcing nor a fortress.

structure.reason: Flank opening with the centre left undecided.

approach.reason: Respectable at strong level, used less than main lines.

plans.reason: Both sides fianchetto and fight for small edges.
